summary: Finite crate-private OTLP metrics, traces, logs, common, resource, and collector message authority for the owned protobuf kernel. The complete bounded 43-message source slice, unit-test bodies, and terminal native default-plus-metrics library check are present; unit-test execution, reference bytes, the feature matrix, and runtime integration remain pending.

wire_schema_release.authority_rule: The v1.10.0 release identity plus every vendored source digest below is binding. The wrapper repository commit is not represented as an upstream schema commit.

wire_contract.byte_identity_claim: Known canonical encodings are deterministic. Decode and re-encode preserves every unknown raw field byte but does not claim to preserve its original position among known fields.

evolution_contract.string_index_fields: AnyValue tag 8 and KeyValue tag 3 are modeled exactly because they are present in v1.10.0; adapters outside profiles may leave them at zero but may not repurpose them.

resource_contract.merge_failure_atomicity: A merge API may claim all-or-nothing failure only if it decodes into staging state and commits after complete validation. An in-place incremental merge must instead document and test its partial-mutation-on-error contract.
resource_contract.producer_truncation_boundary: Producer adapters may apply stricter truncation or drop policies only when their existing contract defines a dropped counter. The schema codec itself never silently truncates, drops, or treats zero as unbounded.

generic_wire_limits.source: ProtobufWireLimits::default() from the 4 MiB gRPC default

shared_semantic_budget.accounting: All nested messages share one context. Counts are charged before reserve/push; string and bytes lengths are charged before allocation; unknown raw bytes are charged once; checked arithmetic only.

limit_provenance: 4 MiB message, 65,536 field, depth 100, and 4x work limits are current owned generic-wire defaults.
128 attributes and 4,096 value bytes are current owned logs limits.

The 128 span attributes/events values are conformance-test helper defaults only. The simplified/testing OtlpSpan exporter has an unbounded attribute Vec, no events collection, and a distinct 255-character value truncation, so trace attribute/event/link schema caps are new A3 policy relative to that exporter.
1,000 points per metric aligns with current max_cardinality; 4,096 metrics aligns with current max_metrics.
128 links is the already-recorded future cap in the span-link cardinality audit; current producer wiring has no link cap and cannot migrate until it chunks or rejects explicitly.

Resource/scope/record, recursive AnyValue, trace attribute/event/link, exemplar, bucket, quantile, and string-path caps are new A3 policy and require downstream migration proof rather than an incumbent-parity claim.
resource_contract.semantic_invariant_completeness: NON_EXHAUSTIVE_MINIMUM. Implementations remain bound to every normative requirement in the pinned v1.10.0 sources; a validator must not treat this list as the complete semantic specification.
required_semantic_invariants: A span trace_id is a nonzero exact 16-byte value and span_id a nonzero exact 8-byte value; parent_span_id is empty or exactly 8 bytes.
Log and exemplar trace_id are empty or exactly 16 bytes; span_id is empty or exactly 8 bytes. Link IDs are exact nonempty widths.
Span and span-event names are nonempty. Span start_time_unix_nano and end_time_unix_nano are nonzero, and the end is not earlier than the start.
Nonempty span and link trace_state values use W3C tracestate syntax with no duplicate keys, at most 32 members, key and value component limits, and the recorded 512-byte aggregate cap.
Attribute keys are unique within each owner collection where the pinned schema requires uniqueness.
Histogram bucket_counts is empty with empty bounds or has exactly explicit_bounds length plus one; explicit bounds are strictly increasing; count equals the checked sum of bucket_counts.
Exponential histogram positive and negative bucket arrays each obey their cap and count equals zero_count plus positive and negative buckets when representable.
Summary quantiles are finite, in the closed interval 0 through 1, strictly increasing, and unique.
Summary quantile values are not negative.
Partial-success rejected counts are nonnegative; zero with a nonempty message is accepted as a warning and a positive count with an empty message is accepted.
Unknown enum values and unknown flag bits survive decode and re-encode even when semantic helpers do not interpret them.

current_authoring_gaps: derive-generated nested and map encoding starts fresh default wire budgets rather than sharing the parent depth and work context
derive-generated repeated, packed, and map decoding allocates and pushes without a per-collection pre-allocation count check
packed and map encoding can collect a complete source collection before the parent message limit rejects it
derive-generated oneof decoding replaces a repeated message-valued member instead of merging the same member as protobuf requires
the proc-macro feature is optional and metrics does not imply it; no-default-features plus metrics must compile
the macro expansion's ::asupersync path is not a production self-alias in the current crate
compatibility UnknownFields::record and record_raw retain ordinary Vec growth; fallible alternatives exist, but a safe downstream shared nested-writer authoring surface remains pending
implementation_contract.allowed_resolution: The complete common/resource/metrics/trace/logs/collector slice uses manual finite-message ProtoMessage implementations with one shared semantic budget and reviewed bounded nested/collection primitives in the owned authoring layer. Every path must check count, depth, work, and payload bytes before its corresponding allocation or mutation. Fresh decode may build private staging state and returns no partial model. Any merge API must either stage and commit atomically or explicitly document and test its non-atomic partial-mutation behavior.
implementation_contract.forbidden_resolution: Derive the current messages and apply validate() only after decode, or encode nested messages into unconstrained temporary buffers, then claim pre-allocation limits.
implementation_contract.signal_construction_separation: Adapters from MetricsSnapshot, trace batches, and LogsSnapshot remain separate from the schema types and are owned by downstream integration beads.

feature_contract.expectation: Additive source-compatible generic protobuf authoring errors and fallible methods are present; no generated OTLP reference dependency or public OTLP schema type is added.
Private owned schemas compile on native targets without opentelemetry-proto, tonic, or tokio normal edges.
The same owned schema module compiles; generated reference messages remain test/fuzz oracle-only.
Private owned schemas compile without assuming the optional proc-macros feature.
The generated oracle remains quarantined; its stale lock must be refreshed by its owner before it can claim v0.32 parity. A3 does not modify the fuzz lock.
Native OTLP finite-schema integration remains excluded unless a later owner supplies a wasm-safe wire boundary and evidence.

no_claim_boundaries: This packet records source, unit-test bodies, and a terminal native default-plus-metrics library check for the complete private 43-message common/resource/metrics/trace/logs/collector slice; it does not execute the unit tests.
It does not represent any valid, malformed, resource, property, differential, or fuzz vector as passing evidence.
It does not prove byte parity with opentelemetry-proto, another language, or a live collector.
It does not wire metrics, traces, logs, partial-success responses, HTTP, gRPC, retry, cancellation, batching, or shutdown.
It does not establish incumbent parity for the new A3 semantic limits; downstream adapters must prove chunking, rejection, or counted truncation per capability.
It does not add opentelemetry-proto, tonic, tokio, or another runtime to a production graph.

It adds only the recorded source-compatible generic protobuf authoring methods and non-exhaustive error variants; it adds no public OTLP schema type and removes or narrows no generic downstream capability, feature, target, persisted format, or user journey.
It does not authorize removing prost, opentelemetry, opentelemetry_sdk, or any generated differential oracle.
It does not authorize production cutover, transport integration, dependency retirement, or tracker closure.

It does not prove performance, allocation, RSS, throughput, latency, broad workspace health, release readiness, live RCH fleet availability, local Cargo fallback approval, or permission to delete files.
